quickStarts.text:
The user is watching iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 26.0) in the Device panel.
Drive it with /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device. It is bound to this device and session, so it needs no --platform, --udid, --serial, --config or --session flags. Use this exact path; login shells may reset PATH.
Every app launch, deep link, tap, text entry, alert, setting, screenshot and recording on this device goes through it. Run open <bundle-or-package-id> (apps lists them) before snapshots, CLI screenshots or input; it starts the session they need. Use device_screenshot just to look.
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device open <bundle-or-package-id> --relaunch  # restarts the app; Expo dev clients connect to their Metro, --metro-port <port> picks it
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device open <bundle-or-package-id> <deep-link-url>
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device snapshot -i  # accessibility tree with @eN refs
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device press @e3 --settle
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device fill @e5 "text" --settle
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device alert accept
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device settings appearance dark  # also text-size, permission grant <name>
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device screenshot /tmp/shot.png  # iOS saves 1x points; add --pixel-density <n> (3 on most iPhones) for device resolution, or call device_screenshot to look
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device record start --scope device /tmp/run.mp4  # then record stop
  /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device install <app> <path-to-.app-or-.apk>
Prefer snapshot refs over coordinates. Run /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device help <command> for flags and /state/device/targets/t3-abc/agent-device help workflow for guides.
Do not use simctl, idb, adb or ssh for those actions. They stay fine for builds, installs, code sync, Metro, port forwards, logs, test runners and what this command cannot do; come back to it for every UI action and screenshot so the user can watch.
Each device_open returns its own command; opening another device does not retarget this one.
The command is removed when the device closes or Conn restarts. If it is missing, call device_open again.
First use builds an XCTest runner and can take a couple of minutes; later commands are fast.
